faq.a: Sohrab is associated with the Persian form سُهْرَاب, whose core sense is sohrab; a persian legendary hero.

faq.q: What is the origin of Sohrab?
faq.a: Sohrab is associated with Persian. Sohrab is Persian سهراب (Sohrāb), the name of a hero in the Shahnameh. It is used as a male given name in Iran.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Sohrab can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sohrab should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Sohrāb is a Persian name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Sohrab mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sohrab is rendered سہراب and carries the sense سہراب، فارسی ہیرو.

faq.q: What does Sohrab mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sohrab is rendered سهراب and carries the sense سهراب، پهلوان ایرانی.
A romanized syllable approximation is soh-rab. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sohrab?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sohrab, sohrab. Script forms are سهراب, سُهْرَاب, سہراب, सोहराब.

faq.q: Is Sohrab a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
